transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Kellerman (Head of ML, Catalyst Retail), Maya Li (Platform Engineer), Samir Patel (CTO)

Summary: brief check-in on pilot results, discuss canary plan (10% traffic), rollback criteria, runbook ownership, and finalize next steps for go-live. Agreed to 24h canary, metrics to monitor: p50/p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, and end-to-end SLO.

Topics: results review; tuning/quantization tradeoffs; canary & cutover plan; monitoring & dashboards; runbook/playbook; security/SAML; pricing follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Blake: hey everyone, thanks for making time, um we'll kick off, quick agenda, results summary and then priya will run through the canary plan.
[00:18] Tom Kellerman: sounds good, Jordan. we ran the batch tests last week, we saw p50 around 110ms on the hosted path, p95 spiked to 720ms during concurrency, and the cost estimate is within the ballpark but we want to validate at scale.
[00:35] Priya Shah: yea, so the numbers you saw map to our env -- initial mis-config on batching size which we tuned, we also tried the int8 quant profile on the dedicated pool which dropped median latency by about 20% but increased token variance slightly.
[00:52] Maya Li: quick q, when you say int8, is that Redwood's quant or the model quant shipped? also any impact on accuracy? we saw one hallucination bump in a rerank job.
[01:10] Priya Shah: it's our runtime-level quant path, so quantized kernels at inference; accuracy impact was minimal on the evaluation prompts we ran but we flagged a small regression on the branded-entity prompts, we captured diffs in the eval sheet (link shared).
[01:27] Samir Patel: okay, that regression is concerning if it hits production, we need guardrails. what's your recommended approach for canary to detect quality regressions early?
[01:44] Priya Shah: two pronged: 1) functional canary with synthetic prompt set mirroring top user intents, run at 10% traffic; 2) shadow traffic to dedicated variant with continuous eval scoring (we'll compute rouge/embedding-sim delta on a 5-min cadence). If the quality delta exceeds threshold, auto-failover to hosted stable model.
[02:10] Tom Kellerman: auto-failover sounds good. what thresholds would trigger rollback? error rate >0.5% or quality delta more than 3% on our eval metric?
[02:26] Jordan Blake: recommended rollback: error rate >0.5% or p95 latency >1.2s for more than 5 minutes, or quality delta >3% for two consecutive windows. we can tune numbers with you but that's the default we're proposing.
[02:44] Maya Li: network question: if we use Redwood Private in our VPC, how does cutover work? any brief on connection handoff?
[03:00] Priya Shah: for VPC we do blue/green at the load balancer level, we update routing rules to point to the new cluster; connection draining is configured. if it's Dedicated with shared control plane, we push traffic routing policies via the route table, so cutover is a policy change not redeploy.
[03:20] Tom Kellerman: do we need any infra changes on our side for prefix caching or KV cache eviction? we currently operate an LRU cache in front.
[03:33] Priya Shah: no infra changes required, Redwood can respect your cache headers and TTLs, but we recommend exposing the KV-cache TTLs in the runbook so ops can correlate. tiny note: transcript generator sometimes shows K V cash, haha.
[03:52] Jordan Blake: (laughs) yep that happens. okay let's talk schedule. we propose starting a 24 hour canary next Tuesday with 10% of sessions for the customer cohort. Priya will run the canary and monitor metrics.
[04:08] Tom Kellerman: timeline wise, our preferred go-live is before Dec 18; doable?
[04:16] Jordan Blake: yes, if canary is green and the runbook review completes. next we need SSO config for SAML sign-on test and a network diagram. Maya?
[04:26] Maya Li: I'll share SAML metadata and a VPC peering diagram by Friday, we've got a security review next week too.
[04:33] Samir Patel: also, we need to validate KMS integration for key rotation — is that handled in Redwood Private or do we bring our own HSM?
[04:44] Priya Shah: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; we can rotate keys on schedule; we'll put the integration steps in the runbook.
[04:52] Jordan Blake: moving on to monitoring, we'll provide a dashboard in the Console: per-route p50/p95, token counts, cost per 1k tokens, and error rate. Priya, can you confirm which dashboards you'll share?
[05:06] Priya Shah: yes, two dashboards: 1) Canary overview (latency, error rate, QPS, cost) and 2) Quality regression (eval score diffs and sample failures). we'll share Grafana links and a CSV export endpoint.
[05:22] Tom Kellerman: on alerting, we want a Slack webhook for P1s and a pager duty for ops. can Redwood integrate?
[05:30] Priya Shah: yes, we support Slack webhooks and PagerDuty. will add runbook steps that include alert routing and on-call rosters.
[05:40] Maya Li: concerning canary user segmentation: we want canary only for internal users first, then expand to 10% of external traffic. is that supported?
[05:52] Jordan Blake: yep, canary targeting supports user attributes. we can scope by header, cookie, or user id. we recommend internal users first then phased expansion.
[06:03] Samir Patel: pricing question: if we go Dedicated, how do discounts apply for reserved capacity? we need a monthly commit number; also how do we handle overage?
[06:15] Jordan Blake: reserved capacity contracts give a unit price with overage at the committed rate plus a 20% surcharge when bursting beyond commit; Jordan mentions he'll send a pricing sheet.
[06:28] Tom Kellerman: what's the rollback time window? in our ops playbook we need an expected RTO.
[06:34] Priya Shah: our rollback is immediate by routing back to stable variant; expected RTO under 2 minutes for traffic cutover, full state reconciliation might take longer for caches ~5-10 minutes.
[06:47] Maya Li: runbooks: can we get a sample runbook? we want step-by-step cutover checklist and post-mortem template.
[06:55] Jordan Blake: yes we'll share the runbook template and incident playbook link (shared: https://redwood.ai/pilot-runbook).
[07:05] Tom Kellerman: on security docs, can you send SOC2 attestation and network hardening notes?
[07:12] Jordan Blake: will send SOC 2 Type II and the private deployment security whitepaper.
[07:20] Samir Patel: about QA: if we see subtle quality regressions, can we route only low-risk intents through the new model?
[07:28] Priya Shah: yes, route-level rollout and A/B by route is supported; you can target specific intent classifiers to the stable model while sending others to the canary.
[07:40] Tom Kellerman: let's define success criteria for the pilot: 24h canary green, p95 < 600ms, error rate <0.3%, quality delta <2% on eval set, runbook approved by ops. Agree?
[07:57] Samir Patel: agree, but reserve right to extend canary if edge cases show up.
[08:04] Jordan Blake: good. quick recap of next steps: Priya runs canary, Jordan sends pricing and docs, Maya shares SAML and network diagram. we'll regroup after the canary.
[08:18] Tom Kellerman: any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:22] Priya Shah: none; we just need the SAML metadata and the list of internal test users.
[08:30] Maya Li: I'll send test users and metadata by Fri.
[08:34] Jordan Blake: great. Jordan closing: thanks everyone, we'll track action items in the CRM and send calendar invite for runbook review.
[08:44] (call ends)
